# P30.3 (GO-LIVE.3): national export + public cut-over — SIG is live on surveillancegraph.org

Implements `docs/tickets/P30.3__national-export-and-public-cutover.md` (Round 8). Stacked on
`devin/p30-2b-geospatial-camera-site-resolution` (PR #134). Requirement ids: SIG-LIC-004a/005/006,
SIG-EXPORT-005/006, SIG-GEO-013, SIG-UI-036/037/038/044/047/050, SIG-METRIC-007/008/009/010, §19.4, §42.3.

## Summary

The national real-data surface is **live** on `https://surveillancegraph.org` and the `sig-web` run.app
origin, built from the settled, materialized hosted spine, under the operator's HG-11 launch go (2026-09-23)
and the 2026-09-24 share-alike answer. Every layer is on the one public site (an ODbL 4.4(b) produced work with
"© OpenStreetMap contributors"), while the downloads stay **licence-separated compartments** — ODbL is never
merged into the CC-BY graph. The binding safety framing held at every step; nothing needed a halt.

Headline as rendered on both origins (exactly as the export computes it over its own sites):
**"227998 resolved sites (from 230330 observation-level records; dedup ratio 0.010)"** — with "2332
same-device merges were auto-written …; 11235 proposed merges await human review and are not counted.
Resolution rests on a provisional eval (LLM-bootstrapped gold set; D-R6.1-EVAL, OPEN)."

## What changed

- **ADR-106** supersedes ADR-096 §Decision 1: share-alike is no longer a reason to restrict; an artifact is
  public iff it carries ONE known licence, no recorded exclusion, and agrees with its registered compartment.
  `ops/src/ops/publish.py`: `restriction_reason` (mixed-licence / unknown-licence / excluded / compartment
  mismatch), `assert_public_clean` re-proves one licence per public compartment, `write_licence_index`
  (`LICENCES.json`), `strip_non_public_web` (`/curate/` is not public).
- **Export** (`exports/src/exports/spine_export.py`, `shaping.py`): per-(source, rights) slicing for a source
  with several rights records (the hosted `dot_511_ky` CC0 + public-record mix stopped the fail-closed gate);
  `web/map.json` labelled with every licence it draws on (→ a restricted build input, never a download) and
  never carrying a refused subject; tiles filed under their own compartment; freshness dates the spine does not
  record publish as the explicit `not-recorded` token; dossier action blocks in full shape, explicitly unknown;
  map absence reasons in the web vocabulary.
- **In-GCP export** (`ops/gcp/export.sh`): Cloud Run job `sig-export` on a tagged image (never `:latest`),
  writing into the private restricted bucket; `fetch` pulls it to `exports/out/national`.
- **Web**: map island fetches `/map/points.json` (225,105 points) instead of inlining them; the maplibre v6
  worker is bundled (`?worker&url` + `setWorkerUrl`) — it 404'd since P27.9, so the island never drew a point;
  `data-drawn` e2e; per-compartment tile sources in `/map/style.json`, each attributed; a real-data build never
  renders the committed OKC demo constants (optional `web/presentation/*.json` only the fixture harness ships),
  and the site-wide "How we know this" is derived from the export.
- **Tasks**: `sig-tasks osm-feed pull --no-feed` — the honest 0-of-0 leverage metric for the public build
  (never the recorded fixture changesets).

## Design decisions

- Exported in GCP (10.5 min, 4 CPU / 16 GiB next to Cloud SQL) — the laptop fetched the snapshot in ~90 s but
  could not hold the build under memory pressure.
- `sig-web` is `nginx` over a gcsfuse mount of the `…-sig-web` bucket (verified), so the bucket sync **is** the
  deploy — no new revision. The web sync mirrors the build exactly (removes the OKC demo pages); the prior site
  is kept privately for rollback.
- Mixed-licence render inputs stay private; the per-licence compartments are the downloads (4.6 offer).

## Review

An independent fresh-context review found no blocker; fixed: site-vs-partition guard
(`assert_site_matches_partition`), unregistered compartments never public, publish refuses fixture
presentation data, `--no-feed`/`--fixtures` exclusive, several nits. `/map/points.json` (the site's rendering
data, all compartments) is recorded explicitly in ADR-106 §5 and flagged to counsel (D-P30.3-COUNSEL).
